doc: Deferred negatives (debt D7 -- docs/verdict_policy.md Section 6). Positive cases whose verdict guard IS expect-flippable (it compares against an operator-supplied expected value) but which carry no sound NEG_ROW yet, each with an explicit reason. Unlike the conformant-absence registry (DUT-behaviour guards that no --expect can fault), these can and should eventually get a sound expect-flip negative or a parameterisation; the reason records why they don't yet (Linux deviation makes the positive itself fail, the guard checks a compiled constant that must be lifted to applyExpectedDefaults, etc.). Tracked here so the exhaustiveness audit accounts for them rather than letting them fall through. A key is a case_id (every fail final of the case) or CASE:final (one final of a SOUND_ROW case that its row does not reach; docs/tech-debt.md TD-42). A deferral must be its final's only account. Prefer fixing over deferring.

cases.ARP_33:udp_eth_dst_is_mac1_not_mac2: the same wall as its ARP_35 sibling below, and harder: ARP_33 injects TWO gratuitous Responses, so under docs/tech-debt.md TD-32 lwIP creates no entry from either and the case never reaches a UDP egress at all -- it is a platform_known_fail here, landing dut_arp_request_after_double_injection instead. No flip reaches this final either: setting arp.tester_mac to the real MAC2 would make the guard match, but `pass` (== tester_mac2) is earlier in document order and takes the run, and the case's one row slot is already spent on udp_eth_dst_neither_mac1_nor_mac2
cases.ARP_35:udp_eth_dst_is_mac1_not_mac2: expect-flippable in principle (the guard compares the egress MAC against --expect arp.tester_mac) but not by any single flip: setting arp.tester_mac to the real MAC2 does make the guard match, yet `pass` (== tester_mac2) is earlier in document order and takes the run, and the case's one row slot is already spent on udp_eth_dst_neither_mac1_nor_mac2. Nor can a fault produce it: ARP_35 leads with a gratuitous Response and docs/tech-debt.md TD-32 records that lwIP etharp creates no entry from one, so there is no first MAC to keep and both ignore-flavours find nothing to swallow. Its ARP_32 / ARP_34 siblings, whose first injection is a Request, carry that final's negative instead
